summary: Design transaction tests, triage exceptions and document audit evidence. Explore the practical continuous controls monitoring course.
lede: Continuous controls monitoring uses transaction data and defined rules to flag activity that may indicate control problems. For internal auditors, finance controllers and risk analysts, it provides a repeatable way to test payments, expenses, procurement and revenue. The course covers checking data in Excel, setting risk-based rules and thresholds, prioritizing exceptions, and documenting follow-up in an auditable monitoring plan.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who own, test, investigate or provide assurance over recurring financial transactions and their controls.
modules: COSO Control Objectives and Monitoring Scope
prerequisites: Working familiarity with finance, internal audit, risk, compliance or transaction-processing controls is expected. No coding or programming is required; exercises use sample transaction data and Excel-based analysis. Advanced analytics and automated monitoring are introduced at an operational-awareness level, while rule design, triage and plan documentation receive hands-on practice.
